decision: Which homepage model should savargupta.com use: structured index, object desk, or a hybrid?
primary_axis: page structure / navigation model (scannable index vs. objects-as-navigation)
invariants: same content and facts (see DESIGN.md content invariants)
same section set: about, projects, writing, travel, food (Beli), coffee chat (Cal.com), resume
same generated object and photo assets reused across B and C

options.bet: A calm, scannable one-column page wins the 20-second visit
options.benefit: Fastest read for recruiters; easy to build and maintain; ages well
options.cost: Low personality; the travel and food side of Savar reads as a footnote
options.risk: Looks like many other student portfolios

options.bet: A playful desk of objects makes the site memorable and invites exploration
options.benefit: Distinct; shows taste and the life outside work (travel, food, coffee)
options.cost: No facts on the first screen; every answer is one click away; heavy image assets
options.risk: Recruiters bounce; mobile needs a separate layout (the reference admits it)

options.bet: Facts on the left, a desk of objects on the right, a structured index below
options.benefit: Scannable first screen plus a memorable, clickable personality layer
options.cost: More complex to build; two navigation systems (nav bar and objects)
options.risk: Can feel like two sites stitched together if the visual language does not unify them
